title: Trace-splitter sidecar: safe backend migration proxy with dedup and latency-preserving fanout
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Implement a lightweight sidecar (trace-splitter) to enable gradual migration from our legacy Jaeger collector to Tempo-based backends. The sidecar will accept OTLP/HTTP and gRPC traces from services, perform de-duplication and idempotent buffering, and fan out to multiple backends while preserving client-observed latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar accepts OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP inputs with TLS
Per-span deduplication using stable-hash keys prevents duplicate ingestion to downstreams
Configurable fanout targets with rate-limited workers and backpressure
End-to-end added p95 latency <= 5ms under normal load
Canary rollout pipeline with automated health checks and rollback on error thresholds
Metrics emitted: duplicate_rate, downstream_latency_p50_p95, buffer_occupancy, dropped_spans
design_decisions: Use stable span-key computed from (trace_id, span_id, start_time, service_name) for deduping; avoid full payload fingerprinting to reduce CPU
Implement in-memory bounded LRU cache with optional Redis-backed cache for long-tail dedupe across restarts
Fanout worker pool per-backend with separate token-bucket rate limits to prevent noisy neighbor downstreams
Expose synchronous 200 to clients after local persist+queued fanout to ensure low client latency while guaranteeing best-effort delivery to all backends
TLS mutual auth supported for enterprise Tempo endpoints; rotate certs via existing KMS workflow
work_items: Prototype sidecar PoC and smoke test (ENG-67210-POC)
Integration tests: dual-write verification and idempotence (ENG-67210-IT)
Load test harness: simulate 100k spans/s, measure p50/p95 overhead
Docs: runbook, migration checklist, console UI flag for toggling fanout
progress_updates: 2026-02-28 - Ticket created; scoping meeting with Observability and Platform teams. Owner: Liam Chen.
2026-03-02 - Design sketch reviewed; decision to use Redis optional dedupe store for long-lived spans. Action: Security review request.
2026-03-05 - PoC implemented (in-process sidecar) and validated in dev cluster. CPU overhead ~2% at baseline. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-sidecar/pull/12

2026-03-09 - Load test showed p95 increase of 3.2ms at 50k spans/s; configured batcher to reduce syscalls and lowered p95 to 2.1ms. Benchmark results: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/trace-splitter/2026-03-09
2026-03-12 - Canary orchestration runbook drafted; initial canary on internal traffic planned for 2026-03-16. Observability dashboards prepared: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/trace-migration
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Duplicate suppression false negatives for reordered spans. Mitigation: include start_time tolerance window and allow post-processing merge.
Risk: Redis backing store introduces latency. Mitigation: make Redis optional and use local cache for hot-path; async enrichment to Redis.
Risk: Increased client-side tail latency under bursty loads. Mitigation: bounded queue with shedding policy and graceful fallback to single-backend write mode.
notes: Coordinate with Security for mTLS cert rotation (ticket SEC-341)
Plan migration playbook with Customer Success for customers on dedicated collectors
Consider future extension to transform/normalize span attributes for legacy clients
